$comment: task-kit depends on plugins-kit:skills-kit for skills_kit_lib (schema_engine and document_walker, hard-imported by the task_system package) and on plugins-kit:awesome-kit because the task CLI's work verb emits Skill(awesome-kit:orchestrate) as the always-required baseline skill; skills-kit and awesome-kit are auto-installed when missing. bootstrap_lib has no direct import here: the vendored bootstrap_guard is stdlib-only and the shared-lib link serves llm_kit, which the review verb imports lazily (CodexCliBackend) to repair summaries and which the dashboard's optional edge (jobs_edge.py, the only dashboard module that names it) imports lazily for autonomous runs, refusing them with a stated reason when it is absent or too old. llm-kit has no install edge, preserving the optional summary-repair policy: without it review refuses repair with an actionable diagnostic. requires_bootstrap matches skills-kit's floor (0.138.0), the newest bootstrap call shape this plugin's hard imports reach. The dashboard (the task-kit command) adds psutil to the venv for cross-platform process identity, and openai because the endpoint helpers it offers to a run are called through the llm-kit shared library, whose OpenAI-compatible transport imports it (a consumer declares the shared library's third-party requirements itself). bin/ is synced to the data directory and that directory is put on PATH (path_entries), so task-kit works in any terminal; the synced copy is a thin locator that runs the newest installed version from the plugin cache, and it uses the marketplace name plugins-kit exactly as the plugin's other data paths do.
